system: Stopping a timer and logging its hours: a screen, the service behind it, and the remote system that keeps the time entries
reports: the message in the stop dialog

places.name: the message in the stop dialog

facts.name: no timer is left
facts.says: when the person presses stop, the service holds no timer for them, as after a stop on another device

facts.name: the timer first started on an earlier day
facts.says: the timer was started before today and left running or paused

facts.name: the person chooses to discard
facts.says: in the dialog the person chooses to discard the timer instead of logging its hours

facts.name: a discard also reads the week again
facts.says: the pages say a write reads the week once, after it lands; they do not say whether clearing a timer without logging counts as such a write

facts.name: the timer is marked from an earlier try
facts.says: an earlier try at this stop got no clear answer from the remote system, and the timer still carries the mark of that stop

facts.name: the earlier try's hours landed
facts.only: the timer is marked from an earlier try
facts.says: the remote system already holds the hours the earlier try sent

facts.name: the hours landed before the answer was lost
facts.only: the remote system gives no clear answer
facts.says: the remote system took the hours, and its answer never arrived

facts.name: the remote system's time entries already has the record
facts.says: the item already has an entry for the day; this is normal, and the hours are added to it

facts.name: the timer was dealt with on another device while the dialog was open
facts.says: a read made while the dialog is open finds the timer stopped or switched elsewhere

facts.name: another log of this timer is in progress
facts.says: the timer's stop is being saved by another request at this moment

facts.name: another device already logged this timer
facts.says: the service answers that the timer was already logged, by a log this screen did not send

facts.name: the item is closed or no longer assigned
facts.says: the timer's item no longer takes time: it is closed, or the person is no longer assigned to it

facts.name: the hours sent are more than 24
facts.says: the dialog's hours field holds more than 24 hours, the most one stop may log

facts.name: the day would pass 24 hours
facts.says: the hours sent, added to what the person's items already hold for the day, come to more than 24

facts.name: the remote system gives no clear answer
facts.says: the write of the hours is sent and no clear answer comes back

seq.says: Stop reads the service's timer first, because this screen's count can be behind a pause or stop on another device.
The dialog shows the item and the hours the timer ran, filled once from the timer just read.

run.says: Discard takes two steps: the person is asked a second time.

otherwise.says: The person checks the hours, may add a note, and confirms or cancels. Nothing is sent before they confirm.

any: a discard also reads the week again

seq.says: The pages do not say whether the checks come before the mark.

rules.rule: The hours saved are the value in the dialog's field, filled when the dialog opens from the timer just read, and not the live elapsed time. The field's stepper moves in quarter hours.

The day sent is today. When the timer first started on an earlier day, the dialog says when it started and offers the days of this week up to today, set to the day it started. One stop logs to one day.
rules.when: the timer first started on an earlier day

rules.rule: The hours are added to the entry the item already has for the day. An entry is never lowered or deleted.
rules.about: add the hours to the entry
rules.when: the remote system's time entries already has the record

rules.rule: A try made again after no clear answer logs the hours the first try recorded, whatever the dialog then holds.
rules.about: add the hours to the entry
rules.when: the timer is marked from an earlier try

rules.rule: The confirmation shows the hours the service answers it logged.
When the item is refused, the dialog says why and offers the list of items, so the same hours can be logged to another item. Any such refusal reads the list of items again.
rules.when: the item is closed or no longer assigned

rules.rule: A refusal for the day's total names the hours the day already holds.
When another device logged the timer first, the dialog says so and keeps what was typed, and the timer and the week are read again.
rules.when: another device already logged this timer
